steps.u: The access-logs bucket keeps everything forever. Per the retention policy (https://confluence.corvid.internal/x/LOGRET2) we need: versioning on, move to Glacier after 30 days, delete after 400. Update the Terraform.

steps.a: Using the separate `aws_s3_bucket_versioning` and `aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration` resources (AWS provider v4+ style). With versioning on, expiring current objects only adds delete markers, so I'll also expire noncurrent versions, or storage would keep growing.

i.command: cd terraform/envs/staging && terraform fmt -check -recursive ../../ && terraform validate

steps.a: Added versioning and a lifecycle rule (Glacier at 30 days, expire at 400, noncurrent versions expire after 30) to the logging module. fmt and validate pass; the staging plan is 2 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. I haven't applied anything.
